Text: Due to Sinus Ardorum's unique aetheric conditions, flora and fauna are on rare occasion greatly enlarged. To investigate this phenomenon further, measurement of aetheric concentration in certain lunar springs and comparison of the average size of fish against the largest specimen is necessary. Aid us in determining the correlation between these factors by delivering the largest fish you reel in during the designated timeframe.

Though the glassy Soda-lime Float continues upstream from the Slumping Plunge, we have as yet limited information on the life cycles of the diverse aquatic life-forms along the entire river basin. Our current studies of the impesctor have revealed that they take on an elongated, fish-like form before attaining greater size, and by examining such large creatures, we are confident that we can achieve a breakthrough. As such, we are requesting the delivery of particularly sizable specimens.

While we were not expecting the forest isles of Auxesia to yield minerals in significant quantities, preliminary investigations have happily confirmed the presence of a variety of metals suitable for producing alloys that meet the initiative's stringent standards. As part of our endeavor to increase self-sufficiency on the star, we call upon our capable artisans to prepare ingots on-site.

Weather phenomena characterized by unusual aetheric turbulence have been observed on Auxesia, not least of all floracanes. These events appear to accelerate the deterioration of foreign metals, and the effect is worryingly pronounced in areas removed from the rainbow crystal. In light of this, we wish to treat metals for aether resistance prior to use─unglamorous work, but critical to our success nonetheless.

While we have been employing new machinery and equipment on Auxesia to great effect, a shortage of replacement parts is all it takes to throw a cosmic wrench in our productivity. To ensure that our work continues hoppingly, we seek to bolster our stockpiles with those components that are in demand at work sites. Your contributions underpin our ongoing exploratory progress, and we ask that you spare no effort.

As the restoration of the city's systems progresses, the magic-based control of vegetation has shown improved capacity, and we expect it will soon effectively keep noxious species in check. Yet though such plants may cause harm, total eradication is not an option, for they are a part of the ecosystem. An appropriate degree of hands-on management is the key, to which end we seek to build up a store of forestry implements.

When investigating Voyager structures, it is critical to identify the invisible flow of aether, otherwise we risk inadvertently causing damage to ancient relics. To that end, we wish to develop a portable aetheric gauge which will be distributed to our researchers on the front lines of exploration. We would be duly grateful for contributions of components such as lenses, as well as the production of the instruments themselves.

Our newly deployed logging machina are powerful and effective at their tasks, but by the same token, they undergo extreme wear and require frequent, time-consuming servicing. This has resulted in low utilization rates, and the growing calls for harder-wearing components come as no surprise. We ask our artisans to employ their skills to produce durable replacement parts that can withstand rigorous use.

While we have identified magical passageways in structures like the Sprouting Towerling, these routes appear to be traversable only by the Voyagers. If we are to reach the tower's upper sections, we must do so the old-fashioned way and erect scaffolding. As we did not ship in sufficient materials, however, we ask our artisans to produce the shortfall while bearing the star's unique environmental conditions in mind.

Due to the dramatic terrain of the exploration site, the winches fitted on our new machina are nothing short of indispensable for transporting equipment and other heavy items. However, Auxesia's unusual environment is extremely harsh on the metal of the cables, causing premature degradation. It would be a disaster if a cable were to snap at the wrong moment, and we wish to build up a stockpile so as to ensure timely servicing.

As we explore this lush planet, we must be mindful of our impact on the environment. The exhaust fumes emitted by ceruleum engines, for instance, may have an adverse effect on plant life. While lasting harm has yet to be observed, in order to minimize the risk, we have decided to introduce filtering exhaust systems. Their development will require great skill, but we have utmost confidence in our artisans.

The Voyagers left behind many of their vehicles throughout the city, notable among them the Timberdrone, a flying variety whose potential uses we are exploring. While the units appear to have been magically propelled, their inner construction is relatively simple, and it should be possible to restore them with our technology. In order to employ them in the initiative, we call upon our artisans to provide the specified components.

As the restoration of the city's systems progresses, the flow of aether at the exploration site has become increasingly complex and stratified. Our researchers toil to shed light on its workings, but they are sorely shorthanded. We wish to lend them a helping paw by developing an advanced aetheric gauge that automatically takes readings. Such an instrument will not be easy to devise, and we are counting on our artisans to rise to the occasion.

Our artisans need hardly be told that the quality of one's tools directly influences productivity. In view of this, we wish to upgrade our equipment based on user feedback, in the hope that it will lead to more efficient exploration. The task will demand great technical expertise, and we humbly ask that you contribute yours, drawing upon the sum of your experiences on the initiative as you carry out the enhancements.

Voyager structures often feature oversized resin glass windows, and our analysis has revealed that they amplify the light waves that plants require for growth. However, the passage of time has seen many a window frame fall into disrepair, and this is where our artisans come in. We ask that you not only restore the windows, but reflect upon the artistry of the Voyagers as you bring your skills to bear.

In coming to the Voyagers' home planet, we have enhanced our understanding of their civilization in leaps and bounds. Among other things, we are now very close to unraveling the secrets of the various implements we discovered on Oizys. Drawing upon our latest findings, we ask you to produce replicas of these relics. Your meticulous craftsmanship will afford us greater insights into Voyager civilization.

Auxesia boasts an abundance of unique flora─each and every species an invaluable resource. Some of the star's native plant fibers, for example, can be woven into highly sought-after ropes. However, before we can distribute these products, the initiative must establish safety standards to prevent potential injury. In order to meet demand and decide upon said standards, we require a surplus of quality handcrafted ropes based on those manufactured at our previous destinations.

Though ages have passed since the Voyagers' disappearance from their city, their architecture remains flawless and free of weathering. We believe our predecessors may have applied a magicked treatment on the materials used in these structures─one that blends hardier resources like metal and glass into their lumber. Our researchers are keen to emulate these feats of engineering, and beseech all able artisans to submit their own experimental samples based on our findings.

Aether circulation was once viewed with great importance in the Voyagers' city. As such, we have utilized aetheric stimulants to quicken our own restoration efforts across the region. Alas, these stimulants have one drawback: they are quickly washed away by the star's natural humidity. To counter this, we mean to employ a resin-based substitute with similar properties, but spreading it throughout the city regularly will require a stable supply from our contributors.

A sweeping study of the region's flora has revealed the possibility that the city's diverse plant life was, in fact, systematically organized in every district. In pursuit of more concrete answers, the research team has opted to assemble miniature gardens, that they might study certain species' symbiotic relationships and environmental impacts on a smaller scale. Naturally, manufacturing the gardens will require sufficient time and resources, and all botanical contributions to this project are welcome as we deepen our understanding of Voyager society.

Many of our researchers upend their lives across the sea of stars and into new habitation modules each time we set course for a new destination. The wear and tear on their furnishings and belongings is inevitable after prolonged use, and many items that were brought in brand-new to Sinus Ardorum have seen better days upon their arrival to Auxesia. As it is our duty to ensure these dedicated workers have their creature comforts met and maintained, we ask all available artisans to aid us in the manufacture of new and improved furnishings.

If you have spent a considerable amount of time on Auxesia, then you are doubtless familiar with the auroral flares that occur in its atmosphere. According to initiative skywatchers, these flares are not, in fact, natural─they are intentional phenomena, devised by the Voyagers for the acceleration of plant growth within the city. While the myriad colors and lights are a feast for the eyes, auroral flares may pose great risk to our delicate machinery. To counteract this, we intend to develop a unique variety of parasol that can shield these fragile instruments from the aurora's rays.

Due to Auxesia's verdant environs, the variety of supplies we consume varies greatly from our previous destinations. Sharp foliage damages uniforms and shoes, while the unique water places extra wear upon our fishing equipment. We proffer our hands out to those who can craft improved equipment with the star's natural features in mind, as we will require as many contributions as possible for the research teams' continued endeavors.

Preliminary tests have revealed that Auxesian plant life is especially susceptible to changes in humidity and temperature, and will wither away if not properly preserved. As a result, improvements to our freight transport systems will be necessary if we wish to ship harvested specimens safely to Etheirys. We petition the aid of deft and eager volunteers willing to enhance the freight units' capabilities and push our technology to the pinnacle of its potential.

In a fortuitous development, we have discovered resin-rich fatwood resources on Auxesia, similar in quality to that of Oizys. When one considers the limited ceruleum we can transport from star to star, this discovery is a boon to all who yearn for a fuel supply closer to home. The key to combustible success, then, will be the creation of an accessible and environmentally friendly fuel with these resources, and we implore our contributors to lend their expertise to the development process. As this star is more...flammable than most, we plan to train users in the fuel's potential risks and inform them that it is meant primarily for short-term use.

Our arsenal of initiative-developed equipment shares one inspiring quality─each and every invention has been ingeniously developed from locally sourced materials, no matter the star's environs. We intend to push these innovations to the limit here on resource-rich Auxesia by fashioning much-needed equipment from its flora, such as purified biofuel and specialized uniforms for researchers and explorers. Our staff encourages as many submissions as possible, as we would like to promptly deliver these new creations to all who require them.

The flow of aether was of paramount importance in Voyager society, which prided itself on its sophisticated magicks. In fact, a scan of the city's core infrastructure has revealed intricate webs of catalysts with varying aetheric conductivity, including three-dimensional arcane geometries within some structures. To more thoroughly ascertain the ins and outs of this technology, the research team plans to build miniature versions of these structures for experimentation. They have requested all able procurers to supply us with the materials to accommodate their needs, such as resins and fibers.

We have received new blueprints from our research team, all drafted with a similar goal in mind─to utilize the wealth of knowledge and concepts we have devised over the course of this initiative. Within these drafts are plans for sustainable biofuel, climate-resistant cosmic suits, and lightweight suits for our pilots, among other flawless ideas. To those experts who are keen to break boundaries and see these dreams into reality with us, we seek your support and your expertise now more than ever.

We have received new blueprints from our research team, all drafted with a similar goal in mind─to utilize the wealth of knowledge and concepts we have devised over the course of this initiative. Within these drafts are plans for alchemical solutions to improve plant growth, high-durability suits for our pilots, and flexible-yet-lightweight suits for our higher-ranked individuals, among other flawless ideas. To those experts who are keen to break boundaries and see these dreams into reality with us, we seek your support and your expertise now more than ever.

We have received new blueprints from our research team, all drafted with a similar goal in mind─to utilize the wealth of knowledge and concepts we have devised over the course of this initiative. Within these drafts are plans for more efficient purified biofuel, powersuits with strengthened output capabilities, and high-quality admiral suits for celebratory purposes, among other flawless ideas. To those experts who are keen to break boundaries and see these dreams into reality with us, we seek your support and your expertise now more than ever.

Certain rare plants on Auxesia reinforce their fibers with metals, making them a valuable resource in the verdant metropolis. The material would doubtless have many applications in our work, and, as luck would have it, the research team has demonstrated that certain reagents can be used to extract the mineralized fibers. We call upon our artisans skilled in preparing plants and herbs to turn their hand to the task!

The abundant plant life on Auxesia suggests ample water resources. Indeed, we have uncovered plentiful wellsprings and suspect the lowlands to contain rivers and wetlands. Alas, water may be everywhere, but not a drop to drink. In its natural state, Auxesian water contains elements that are harmful when ingested by thirsty members of the initiative. It is imperative that we purify and sterilize a robust stockpile of usable water.

For time immemorial, we Loporrits have needed nothing more than a nibble on a carrot to revitalize and sustain ourselves. Now, through the Cosmic Exploration Initiative, we have experienced firstpaw the myriad cuisines enjoyed by the people of Etheirys. Should we not likewise explore the untapped potential of the humble carrot? In an effort to provide our Loporrit contributors in the field with a convenient and satisfying snack, we turn first to the development of carrot-flavored pellets.

It has been observed that the children of Etheirys find a well-trimmed lawn as soothing as we Loporrits find a carrot patch calming. Fortunately, there are several such grassy locales within the bounds of our survey area, presenting ideal sites for relaxation facilities. We seek to provide picnicking sets for outdoor dining and gently scented candles to maximize the morrow's motivation!

Though home to a myriad of botanical specimens, Auxesia is distinctly lacking in herbivores and the fruiting plants that might support such species. Nevertheless, the potential for nutritious provisions is found in even roots and leaves. Such Auxesian extracts may even pave the way to a foodstuff of nutritional efficiency and popularity second only to Archon loaf!

The import of foodstuffs via the *Galactic Way* has vastly improved, allowing diners in the habitation module refectory to select from limited meal options. There remains the issue, however, of improving portable provisions for contributors working in the field. Used to a certain level of luxury at the base, contributors are now demanding that their field provisions should have at least some level of flavor. We are requesting the aid of skilled artisans to meet these unreasonable expectations!

Our previous expeditions demonstrated that natural resources can be processed into a wide array of materials, and this is equally true on Auxesia. Preservatives and adhesives from plant oils, spices to simultaneously preserve food and add flavor─our researchers may have near-endless ideas, but are sorely lacking in the skills to translate them into reality. Any contributors available to process raw materials are greatly encouraged to do so.

Auxesian architecture seems to rely heavily on incorporating plant life, which means we must be especially vigilant that our activities do not have any adverse environmental effects. As such, we have decided to use easily disassembled biomaterials in the construction of our base. Natural materials require specific methods of processing, and we are requesting the support of skilled contributors to ensure that all materials meet our safety requirements.

With work on Auxesia progressing apace, some teams are planning a celebration of our efforts thus far. It has come to our attention that several contributors─who have been known to enjoy a drink─are planning to commemorate the occasion by brewing a spirit from Auxesian flora, before sending the completed product to Etheirys. Connoisseurs from across Etheirys will no doubt flock to buy the liquor from a distant star, and we cannot leave this matter to amateurs. Expert artisans are called upon to create the finest vintage, befitting the initiative's name!

Contributors working at isolated outposts on Oizys heaped praise on our self-heating lunches, and there is a similarly high level of demand on Auxesia. Given the proliferation of plant life and damp environs, we think it prudent to improve both the heating element and the preservatives utilized. To protect the star from unintended fires─and the stomachs of our contributors from spoiled food─we are requesting the cooperation of experts in both fields. Rest assured, quality control will be *rigorously* conducted.

In their voyage across the stars, our research team has continued to seek the answer to the question: what makes the perfect, all-purpose yeast? In a dramatic development, yeast derived from strains found in Sinus Ardorum demonstrated unprecedented activity when exposed to the auroral flares of Auxesia. This opportunity must be seized with both paws! The ultimate yeast, effective throughout the universe, is within our grasp.

The initiative issues a challenge to its expert alchemists and culinarians! Your skills, finely honed through countless contributions, lead here: the development of the ultimate formula to stimulate aetheric circulation in an urban environment; and the ultimate cosmic ration, providing a nutritionally complete meal three minutes after the simple addition of boiling water. This is the very pinnacle of progress!

Construction on Auxesia utilizes biomaterials where possible, to preserve the natural environs. The knowledge and experience gained in this process will no doubt prove invaluable in applications far beyond this star. Thus far, two items have been deemed suitable for further research and development: glass blocks made from processed resin, and rations made from nutrient-dense Auxesian beans.

Cosmic tool research is entering its final stage here on Auxesia, and the engineering team is struggling to fulfill demand for the required materials. Researchingway has turned to you─now indisputably the most experienced artisan in the known universe─to complete the ultimate catalyst, described in exacting and near-incomprehensible detail in the inventive Loporrit's notes.

Astounding as it is that the forest isles are supported by great trees which tower several hundred yalms from the surface, it is also of great interest that different strata and forests of varying size have formed upon them. One cannot help but contemplate the months and years that passed before Auxesia's environment reached such a state. In the pursuit of understanding this star further, contributors are requested to visit the designated sites and recover materials. Even the smallest pebble or thinnest blade of grass may hold untold knowledge about the world's history.

Though it is evident that the Voyagers' civilization was one founded on advanced magicks, it is also plain that our methods of gleaning knowledge on the techniques they employed is limited. As crude as it may be, our best means available is to analyze as many samples as possible to find traces of aether. To ensure samples remain unaffected by outside parameters, we ask that contributors gather samples with care and submit them for inspection. Speedy deliveries are particularly appreciated.

As an alien presence on this star, the initiative has undoubtedly influenced the local environment. Whether via potential fungi that may cling to materials used to ensure the safety of members and aid in exploration, or the unintended dispersing of seeds carried from afar, the potentialities are limitless. As such, it is imperative that we gather a large amount of samples as quickly as possible, that we may review materials in their original state. Contributors are encouraged to take the initiative in this effort.

As tests performed on previous expeditions concerning repeated collection of resources within an allocated schedule have yielded highly beneficial data, they will be recommenced on Auxesia. Subjects will be asked to sequentially collect materials from a single location, and their successes will be recorded and analyzed by aerial drones. Please note that by voluntarily participating in this mission, you agree to be observed. *Closely*.

Though we have identified myriad ruins on Auxesia, remnants of the Voyagers' civilization go beyond what is plain to the naked eye. Even now, vestiges of their magicks, and indeed, their Aethernet, yet remain. To perform a more cohesive study of their culture, samples of arcane remnants are essential. Contributors are hereby asked to procure the designated materials within the stipulated time frame. The amount retrieved at the time of gathering will be considered in evaluation.

A manual regarding the concentrated collection of identical resources based on fieldwork in terra incognita has been in the works for some time, and is already being employed by our research teams. Plans to append insights from Auxesia are presently in place, and to aid in this effort, we are recruiting master miners and botanists for the procurement of materials and to provide analytical data. Those who achieve the initiative's goals within the stipulated time frame will be handsomely rewarded.

In the course of our efforts on Oizys, we discovered evidence suggesting that the Voyagers performed careful reduction of materials to increase their purity, just as we do. By performing extractions on the resources available in the heart of their city on Auxesia, we can undoubtedly bring ourselves one step closer to understanding this bygone civilization. The initiative seeks talented contributors to procure the designated resources as quickly as possible.

Amidst the various resources harvested from Auxesia's vegetation, the initiative has identified curious cases of multicolored strains. As we hypothesize that this phenomenon is a result of turbid aether in certain environments, it is imperative that we improve our understanding of the flow of aether in the ruins. In this pursuit, we request contributors to procure high-quality samples of onionroot ore and copycube flowers respectively.

It is theorized that the Voyagers utilized high-level magicks capable of bending natural matter to their will in order to construct the city. Such an endeavor would have required materials highly reactive to aether. The research team has already identified potential items matching this quality, and all that is left is to procure the materials to verify their hypothesis. Contributors are encouraged to put forth their best effort, as those who retrieve high-quality materials will be favorably evaluated.

The initiative has discovered that resources believed to be the product of the Voyagers' purification efforts may have been vital components employed in the functioning of the city's mechanisms. The conductive mediums used in the towerlings and the seeds used as a template in the construction of facilities are examples of this. In the interest of performing practical experimentation, contributors are urged to procure the designated materials by the indicated time.

We have determined that the rare flora found in the western section of Pileus Pergola are, in fact, ancient species from Auxesia's distant past. By examining the annual growth rings of trees in the area and the matter sealed within amber, we can gain a better understanding of the climate and environment throughout the star's history. We have every faith that our talented contributors can procure the research team's desired materials─in bulk─within the stipulated time.

Preliminary research of tortoisepine amber and cerulift logs indicates they will prove essential to understanding the history of the star. The acquisition of even higher quality samples would do much to bolster and accelerate our studies. For this reason, we task contributors with procuring the required materials at the highest quality possible, and to do so within the time stipulated by the research team. Those who can achieve this objective will earn the utmost respect among the initiative.

Through further study of amber and raw timber borne from tortoisepine and cerulift trees, we have developed a working theory that the Voyagers utilized aethersand and tree roots highly conductive to aether as catalysts for their magicks. By examining high-quality samples from as many subjects as possible, we may gain further insight into their methods. We are counting on our talented contributors to aid us in this pursuit.

The ponds of Auxesia are home to a variety of aquatic fauna with plantlike properties. Dubbed “botanifish” by our researchers, these specimens appear to interact favorably with the species the initiative has introduced, leading to hopes that they might readily coexist. In order to test this hypothesis, we call upon willing contributors to quickly procure designated aquatic species for subsequent evaluation.

Each of the forest isles that comprise much of the urban center are effectively isolated in ecological terms. To chart the evolutionary divergence this has caused in the region's aquatic habitats, we are seeking contributors to gather large fish for further study. As we also hope to verify the feeding habits of these specimens, we request that only specified bait is used for the task. Procurement of especially sizable specimens will be handsomely rewarded.

At present, our research teams are conducting an extensive study into the isolated aquatic habitats that dot Auxesia's urban landscape. While an accurate picture of species distribution is slowly emerging, fieldwork is being hampered by the predilection for certain creatures to undergo alarming changes the moment they are hauled out of the water. We are currently looking for contributors unfazed by these quirks to procure research specimens as swiftly as possible.

We believe that Auxesia's botanifish─the star's unique, semi-vegetal aquatic life-forms─hold the key to discovering more about the Voyagers and their tenure here. To this end, our researchers are hastening their study of the creatures, and are urgently seeking further specimens. Contributors will be evaluated based on the quantity of specimens provided, with additional allowances made for quality and size.

Thanks to our diligent researchers and their frankly alarming willingness to ingest unknown species in the name of science, we have discovered that some of Auxesia's aquatic species are edible. As work begins to collect these specimens for use as a food source, we require skilled fishers to catch sufficient supplies. Speed is of the essence here, lest initiative culinarians complain of receiving less-than-fresh specimens on their chopping blocks.

Auxesia's distance from Etheirys presents a unique logistical challenge for the initiative, and further highlights the importance of an efficient supply chain. In the name of efficiency savings, we want to fully optimize the next shipment to Sharlayan─every spare ilm of space in the hold must be utilized. On this occasion, these spare ilms are to be filled with large aquatic organisms bound for the Studium. Contributors will be rewarded for any especially sizable specimens they catch.

Although there are parallels between Auxesia's botanifish and the impesctors found on other stars, the two types of organism are fundamentally distinct. As part of our investigations into these differences, we are examining the dietary habits of botanifish, and are currently seeking to discern optimal baits with which to catch them. To this end, highly skilled contributors are hereby requested to collect large quantities of aquatic specimens using designated baits to help further our inquiries.

In a recent survey, we discovered that many ponds and water features in the region are home to small fishlike mechanisms that interface with the city's myriad systems. The current hypothesis is that these devices─akin to familiars in many regards─were introduced to preserve and maintain the water supply. Contributors are asked to gather samples for further study, paying special attention to collectability.

Measurements indicate that the city's many spires are encircled with aetheric confluences, and are therefore sites of abundant energy. At present, we wish to examine the oversized botanifish that inhabit the waters near the Sprouting Towerling, and thereby determine whether their impressive bulk derives from the aether-rich environment they persist in, or some other factor. Contributors are asked to procure plenty of specimens─the larger the better!

One of our teams specializing in bait research and development has issued a request to all willing initiative fishers. As part of their drive to craft ever more alluring morsels, they seek to determine the impact of specific baits on aquatic fauna, and are thus asking contributors to procure quality samples using designated baits at specified locations.

Among Auxesia's numerous botanifish species, there are some which bloom underwater in spectacular fashion. To better understand this phenomenon, we require a plethora of botanifish samples─blooming and non-blooming varieties included. Contributors are called upon to secure specimens of truly exceptional quality, with rare finds garnering rich reward. Though this is an undeniably difficult task, no doubt our initiative fishers will relish the opportunity to showcase their skills.

Our research teams are currently abuzz with rumors concerning a botanifish that, to quote one commentator verbatim, “looks like a whole bloody garden sprouted fins and started swimming around.” Unsurprisingly, the creature is currently the focus of much scientific curiosity, with many hoping to ascertain what triggers such virulent growth. To aid this study, we request that contributors procure a variety of specimens─both garden-sized and otherwise. Please note that especially prolific fishers will be compensated accordingly.

During a recent fieldwork excursion, one of our research teams detected a highly concentrated aetheric signature emanating from a peculiar form of botanifish. While sheer excitement has propelled much of the investigation into this discovery thus far, additional samples are now required. We ask contributors to procure both legendary botanifish and their more mundane brethren, keeping an eye out for large specimens in particular.

An infestation of plants thought to be of Oizys origin has abruptly sprouted on the isle west of the Timberlodge. The prevailing theory is that stray seeds accompanied our cargo from Terra Firma and had their growth here accelerated by auroral radiation. We seek immediate assistance with the removal of invasive species before they take root in other parts of Auxesia. While incineration is the preferred method, volunteers are requested to harvest foreign specimens by hand in areas where flamethrowers would harm the native vegetation.

We have reports that a pond in the west of the Emerald Nervure has begun glowing, with motes of luminescent aether observed rising from its surface as if in response to the auroral flare. Other bodies of water remain unchanged, the phenomenon seemingly unique to this single location. We suspect aquatic plants are the source of the released energies and have initiated an ecological survey to research any potential applications. Contributors are requested to assist with plant and water sample collection.

We have confirmed the existence of invasive lunar fungi on the Scrambling Ways. The traveling spores were likely attached to freight from Sinus Ardorum, and auroral flares have accelerated their growth tenfold. As we have yet to determine what influence this patch of fungi may pose on Auxesia's climate, we reluctantly turn to the most destructive solution: incineration. Thus, we ready our flamethrowers and implore those with the relevant skill sets to contribute to this combustive cause with all due haste.

We have received numerous reports claiming that an overgrowth of ore-rich fruit has sprouted north of the Timberlodge. While this particular species is generally subterranean, auroral flare activity has pushed its growth to the limit, enabling it to sprout towards the surface. Eyewitnesses report that these rarities retract their roots once the flares subside, so we must make the most of this moment if we wish to harvest and further analyze the crop. Those who can provide drill components and other necessary materials during this time will be well rewarded for their efforts.

According to reports, the floracane caused several vacuum suits working in a remote location to malfunction. Though able to return to the southwestern sector of Pileus Pergola, the rapid unscheduled descent destroyed several key components. The suits will cease all operations for the duration of the floracane to prevent further damage, but repairs will be carried out in situ to allow a swift return to action once the danger has passed. We are requesting urgent delivery of materials directly to the crash site!

What a turn of events! The floracane, on a sweep to remove foreign matter from the city, appears to have had a dramatic effect on the Loporrits. Contact with the aetheric petals induces a strangely intoxicated state, and we are receiving reports that a group of Loporrits working in the field has undergone particularly severe exposure. While Loporrits near the base are protected by the rainbow crystal's influence, this leaves our relief efforts short-pawed. Contributors unaffected by the floracane are requested to provide immediate aid to the victims!

One of our drone fleets has suffered a catastrophic system failure due to recent floracane activity. Data readouts indicate the fleet was operating at low altitude when strong winds blew it outside the rainbow crystal's protective ward. While operators were able to safely land the affected units and thus prevent further damage, the incident has necessitated extensive repairs in situ. Contributors are requested to gather the requisite spare parts for the task.

In addition to wreaking havoc on our instruments and beguiling us with their profusion of color, reports show that floracanes induce a frenzy of microbial activity which helps maintain the balance of Auxesia's ecosystem. Pileus Pergola is currently the epicenter of one such microbial bloom, and we wish to collect fungal spore samples to ascertain its impact on soil quality and local flora. We look forward to your valuable contributions.
